title: Non-local arithmetic rules still behave like local cellular automata

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Non-local arithmetic rules still behave like local cellular automata

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Although arithmetic operations are non-local in digits (carries can propagate arbitrarily far) while cellular automaton rules are local, the overall behavior of number-based systems is very similar to that of cellular automata, so the details of underlying rules do not crucially affect the kinds of behavior that occur.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But despite fundamental differences like this in underlying rules, the overall behavior produced by systems based on numbers is still very similar to what one sees for example in cellular automata.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 4, “Systems Based on Numbers”; section “Elementary Arithmetic” (from p. 117), p. 125. Scope: number-based systems compared with cellular automata and other simple programs

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch04-06: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Large behavioral samples can be computed and compared now. The broad invariance conclusion requires a common non-arbitrary metric and coverage beyond available catalogs, so only selected system families are resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Sample specified arithmetic systems and cellular automata, encode their trajectories using declared invariant features, and compare distributions of behavior classes. Similar distributions across the sampled families support a restricted claim; strong family separation refutes it there.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Sampling and representation choices can determine apparent similarity.

Very similar and kinds of behavior are underspecified.

The conclusion about rule details exceeds any finite comparison.

fields.value:

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Both sides of the comparison are simulable, and one can score arithmetic orbits and cellular automata with one classifier. The claim that the kinds of behavior are very similar, and that rule details therefore do not matter, is a qualitative summary of those pictures rather than a criterion with an obvious refutation. A matched sample is informative and still confounded by how the classes are drawn.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Classify ensembles of simple arithmetic iterations and of local cellular automata with the same behavior taxonomy, and compare the frequencies of repetition, nesting, irregularity, and localized structures. A large, robust difference in those frequencies would challenge 'very similar'; agreement would support it for the sampled families.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Carries are non-local, so a similarity of pictures can coexist with different mechanisms, and both readings fit the same outputs.

'Very similar' and 'do not crucially affect' have no sharp distance between behavior classes.
